children: Kirkland & Ellis on Monday said it hired the co-leader of rival law firm Gibson, Dunn & Crutcher's state attorneys general practice, as U.S. states have increasingly emerged as key regulatory enforcers in consumer protection, antitrust and other areas.

Prerak “Pre” Shah, who was previously senior counsel to Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton and served as acting U.S. attorney for the Northern District of Texas in 2021, has joined Kirkland as a partner in its Houston office, the firm said.
Shah previously served as chief of staff to Republican U.S. Senator Ted Cruz of Texas and worked as his chief counsel on the Senate Judiciary Committee.

Since joining Gibson Dunn in 2021, Shah has been a recurring litigation opponent to the Texas attorney general's office. In December, he represented food industry trade groups in a pending lawsuit against Texas challenging the legality of a new state law that requires warning labels for ingredients like food dyes and preservatives.
Shah was also on the legal team defending BlackRock

in a federal lawsuit filed by Texas and 12 other Republican-led states alleging that BlackRock and other top asset managers violated antitrust law through climate activism that reduced coal production and boosted energy prices.
Federal court records show that Shah is withdrawing from both cases as part of his move to Kirkland.

State attorneys general have become more aggressive in pursuing enforcement and coordinating lawsuits over the past decade. In a publication to clients last month, Gibson Dunn said companies face expanding compliance and litigation risks due to "aggressive enforcement postures" from both Democratic and Republican state attorneys general.
Last week, a group of state AGs secured an $18 billion settlement with Meta Platforms

, resolving claims that the company designed its Facebook and Instagram social media platforms to addict children. Earlier this year, a federal jury in New York found that Ticketmaster and its parent company ​Live Nation
illegally monopolized U.S. live event markets, in a win for bipartisan group of states.

"State AGs are increasingly driving some of the most important disputes facing corporate America. I want Kirkland to be the first call when companies face their most consequential State AG matters," Shah said in a LinkedIn post Monday.
